title: Lumbar FSU sagittal 3x3 stiffness matrix under combined loads: extension, high load

quantity.name: sagittal-plane stiffness matrix (3x3: axial, A-P, flexion-extension)
quantity.definition: 'standing' high-load regime: stiffness fitted from (FH1,FV1), (FH2,FV1), (FH1,FV2), (FH2,FV2). Right-hand Cartesian system of Panjabi et al.: origin at the centre of the SUPERIOR vertebral body in the unloaded state; y axial (vertical), z antero-posterior, theta_x flexion-extension rotation; lower vertebra fixed; sagittal 3x3 stiffness (symmetric, Kij = Kji, 6 distinct coefficients) estimated by least squares from load/displacement differences between combined-load states; all applied loads (incl. deformation-dependent components) resolved to the origin.

source.authors: Edwards WT, Hayes WC, Posner I, White AA III, Mann RW
source.sample: 12 lumbar FSUs (6 L1-L2, 6 L3-L4) from 7 spines T12-S1; 6 loaded in flexion (S16,S18,S21,S03), 6 in extension (S04,S13,S23); n per condition 4-6; fresh-frozen human cadaveric lumbar FSUs (autopsy), no history of spinal surgery/disease

protocol.summary: Dead-weight/cable combined loading: 9 combinations of compressive force (0, FV1, FV2 = ~0, 70, 140% of estimated standing L3 load; FV1 308-400 N, FV2 616-800 N) and horizontal A-P force (0, FH1, FH2 = 1.5 FH1; FH1 234-320 N, sign + for flexion, - for extension), compressive load applied ~30 mm above the vertebral centre; each state held 4 min before displacements were recorded (two steel balls, LVDTs). L1-L2 and L3-L4 not different (P=0.5) and pooled.
how_to_simulate: Fix the inferior vertebra; reference point = centre of the superior vertebral body (unloaded)

Apply the combined sagittal loads of the regime: FV1/FV2 (~310-400 / 620-800 N) compression with FH1/FH2 (~230-320 / 350-480 N) A-P force directed to produce extension (Table 1 gives specimen-specific values)
Record uy, uz, theta_x of the superior vertebral centre for each load state and resolve applied loads to that point
Fit the symmetric 3x3 stiffness (Kyy, Kzz, Ktt, Kyz, Kzt, Kyt) by least squares to the load/displacement differences and compare (convert rad to deg)
protocol.notes: Coordinate system: Right-hand Cartesian system of Panjabi et al.: origin at the centre of the SUPERIOR vertebral body in the unloaded state; y axial (vertical), z antero-posterior, theta_x flexion-extension rotation; lower vertebra fixed; sagittal 3x3 stiffness (symmetric, Kij = Kji, 6 distinct coefficients) estimated by least squares from load/displacement differences between combined-load states; all applied loads (incl. deformation-dependent components) resolved to the origin. Deformation-dependent moment from the offset compressive load is included in the load resolution. Large SD (some SD > mean) reflects specimen variability; flexion stiffer than extension (Kyy significant at both loads).

data.dof: axial force Fy / axial displacement uy
A-P force Fz / A-P displacement uz

extraction.from: Table 2 (p.38); loads Table 1 (p.36); coordinate system p.36-37 and Fig 2
extraction.uncertainty: tabulated values; converted from N·mm/rad and N/rad
extraction.check_notes: All 12 mean/SD values re-read from the rendered Table 2 image. Ktt converted N·mm/rad -> Nm/deg (/57295.8); Kzt, Kyt N/rad -> N/deg (/57.2958). Native values in data[].native.

pass_rule.rule: diagonal terms within mean +- 1 SD; coupling terms sign and order of magnitude
